questions.model:
(a) Rabbit.

questions.q:
Name the process in the carbon cycle that:
(a) converts carbon dioxide into glucose in plants
(b) releases carbon dioxide when coal, oil or gas are burned
(c) passes carbon compounds from a plant into an animal
ms: (a) photosynthesis
(b) combustion
(c) feeding (allow eating / consumption)
questions.tip: The carbon cycle processes in the syllabus: photosynthesis, respiration, feeding, decomposition, fossil fuel formation and combustion.

questions.q:
The table shows the energy in each trophic level of a food chain in one year.
producers: 20 000 kJ
primary consumers: 2 000 kJ
secondary consumers: 180 kJ
(a) Calculate the percentage of energy transferred from the primary consumers to the secondary consumers. [2]
(b) Explain why the transfer of energy between these trophic levels is not efficient. [2]
ms: (b) energy is transferred to the environment as heat (from respiration)
(b) energy used in movement / life processes (respiration)
(b) not all of the organism is eaten (e.g. bones, fur) / some energy lost in faeces (undigested) / some organisms die and are not eaten
questions.model:
(a) 180 ÷ 2000 × 100 = 9 %.
(b) Much of the energy taken in by primary consumers is released in respiration and used for movement, then transferred to the environment as heat. Also, not all parts of the primary consumers are eaten, and some of what is eaten is not digested and is lost in faeces.
questions.tip: Energy is not 'lost' from the universe — it is transferred to the environment, mainly as heat.

ms: grasshoppers decrease because they are eaten by the lizard
frogs decrease because there is less food / competition with the lizard for grasshoppers
snakes eat more rabbits (as there are fewer frogs), so rabbits decrease
foxes decrease because fewer rabbits / more competition with snakes
grass may increase because fewer grasshoppers eat it
questions.model: The grasshopper population would decrease, because the lizards eat them and have no predators to control their numbers. The frog population would then decrease too, because the frogs compete with the lizards for a smaller supply of grasshoppers. With fewer frogs, snakes would eat more rabbits, so the rabbit population might also fall.
questions.tip: Follow the arrows: say which population changes AND why, one link at a time.

questions.q:
Large areas of tropical rainforest are being cut down and burned to clear land for cattle.
Explain how this deforestation can lead to:
• an increase in carbon dioxide in the atmosphere
• loss of soil and flooding
• reduced biodiversity
ms: fewer trees, so less photosynthesis / less carbon dioxide removed from the atmosphere
burning (combustion) of trees releases carbon dioxide
decomposition of remaining wood / leaves releases carbon dioxide (respiration of decomposers)
no roots to hold the soil, so soil is washed / blown away (erosion)
less water absorbed by roots / less transpiration / no leaves to intercept rain, so more run-off and flooding
habitats destroyed so species lose food and shelter
species may become endangered / extinct, so fewer different species (lower biodiversity)
questions.model:
With fewer trees, less photosynthesis takes place, so less carbon dioxide is removed from the atmosphere. Burning the trees releases carbon dioxide by combustion, and decomposers respiring as they break down the remaining wood release more.
Tree roots normally hold the soil together; without them the soil is washed or blown away. Trees also take up a lot of water and their leaves intercept rain, so after clearing more rainwater runs off the land, causing flooding.
Many species lose their habitat, food and shelter, so their populations fall and some become extinct. This reduces biodiversity, the number of different species in the area.
questions.tip: Explain each effect with a cause → consequence chain; just listing the effects is not enough.

questions.q:
The table shows the population of an endangered species of giant tortoise on an island. A conservation programme, including captive breeding, began in 2000.
year:        1970 | 1990 | 2000 | 2010 | 2020
population:  3000 | 1200 |  800 | 1100 | 1600
(a) Calculate the percentage decrease in the population between 1970 and 2000. [2]
(b) Suggest two reasons why the population of tortoises decreased. [2]
(c) Explain how captive breeding and one other conservation method could have helped the population to increase after 2000. [2]
ms: (b) one reason: hunting (for food / shells) / overharvesting
(b) a second reason: habitat destruction (land cleared for farming / housing) / introduced species (e.g. goats competing for food, rats eating eggs) / pollution / climate change
(c) captive breeding: tortoises bred in safe conditions to increase numbers, then young released into the wild
(c) other method: protecting habitats / monitoring the population / education / laws against hunting / removing introduced species (with explanation)
questions.model:
(a) Decrease = 3000 − 800 = 2200. 2200 ÷ 3000 × 100 = 73 %.
(b) Tortoises may have been hunted for food, and introduced animals such as goats may have eaten the plants that tortoises feed on.
(c) In captive breeding, tortoises are bred in safe conditions where the young are protected, and then released into the wild to increase the population. Protecting their habitat, for example by making the island a reserve and removing introduced goats, means the released tortoises have enough food and space to survive.
questions.tip: For percentage decrease, divide the decrease by the ORIGINAL value (1970).
